checkmate-basics.title: Checkmate basics
checkmate-basics.summary: Deliver mate with a rook and a queen.
checkmate-basics.s1: Checkmate ends the game: the king is attacked and has no way to escape, block or capture the attacker.
checkmate-basics.s2: This is a back-rank mate. The rook gives check along the first rank and the black king is trapped behind its own pawns.
checkmate-basics.s3: Your turn: the black king is boxed in by its pawns. Find the checkmate in one move.
checkmate-basics.s4: The king and queen work together. Find the move that checks the king while it cannot capture the queen.

forks.title: Forks
forks.summary: Attack two pieces at once with a knight.
forks.s1: A fork is a single move that attacks two or more enemy pieces. Knights are excellent at it because they jump.
forks.s2: The knight on f7 checks the king and attacks the queen at the same time. Black must save the king, then White takes the queen.
forks.s3: Find the knight move that attacks both the king and the queen.

opening-principles.title: Opening principles
opening-principles.summary: Control the center and develop your pieces.
opening-principles.s1: In the opening, fight for the center, develop your knights and bishops, and get your king to safety.
opening-principles.s2: Play a good first move that fights for the center or develops a piece.
opening-principles.s3: Black has taken space in the center. Develop a knight toward the center.
opening-principles.s4: Well done. Remember: center, development, king safety.

studio.warnBody: This studio builds board themes from colors, gradients, your own textures and the built-in effects. It is not the best way to make themes, and it cannot make 3D piece models, animated pieces or rendered pieces: those need a text editor for theme.json and art tools such as Blender. Use it to start and to learn the format.
studio.previewNote: The preview uses your current pieces.
studio.name: Name
studio.author: Author
studio.needName: Give your theme a name and a valid id (lowercase letters, digits, dashes) first.
studio.bigImage: This image is larger than 6 MB.
studio.guideFormat: A theme is a .cctheme file: a ZIP archive with a theme.json at its root plus images (png, webp, jpg, svg). It is purely declarative: no code of any kind. Everything is validated when you import it: unknown fields, out-of-range values, unsafe paths, fake images and oversized files are rejected with a precise message.
studio.guideFields:
format (must be 1), id, name, version (1.0.0), author, license, description. Then board and/or pieces.
board.view.tilt: camera lean in degrees (0 = top view; above 0 the app renders a real 3D scene). board.lighting: exposure, environment (reflections), key and fill colors. board.scene: background. board.frame: width in squares, paint, bevel, glow. board.squares.light / dark: color, gradient or texture, plus gloss, bevel, grid. board.highlights: style fill / ring / glow and colors. board.ambient: sweep, particles, vignette.
pieces.model: 3D Staunton pieces with white and black materials. Or pieces.source: image sprites with a path pattern containing {piece} (wK, bQ…) and optionally {res} (1x, 2x, 4x), plus baseSize, scale, anchor, offsetY, frames. Both kinds accept shadow, idle (float / breathe / glow / frames), motion (slide / arc / hop, easing, lift, squash, trail, impact) and capture (fade / burst / shatter / dissolve).
studio.guide3dTitle: How to make a 3D theme (the studio can't)
studio.guide3d:
Real 3D is built in: when a theme uses pieces.model, or the board has a tilt above 0, the app renders a real WebGL scene with a perspective camera, lights, shadows and reflections.
1. Procedural pieces. In theme.json set pieces.model to an object with style staunton, a white and a black material, and an optional scale. A material takes color, metalness, roughness, clearcoat, transmission (glass), ior, emissive, emissiveIntensity and opacity. Polished gold: metalness 1, roughness 0.2. Glass: transmission 0.9, roughness 0.05. Ivory: roughness 0.3, clearcoat 0.6.
2. Scene. board.view.tilt (0 to 65 degrees) sets how far the camera leans from the top view. board.lighting sets exposure, reflections and the key and fill colors. The squares, frame and gloss come from what you provide: paint two seamless square textures at 1024 px (light and dark squares) and one for the frame.
3. Animation: pieces.idle, pieces.motion (slide, arc or hop, with trail and impact rings), pieces.capture (fade, burst, shatter, dissolve), board.ambient (particles, light sweep) and board.frame.glow.
4. Your own modeled pieces (Blender or any 3D tool): render the 12 pieces as transparent images from one camera at 1024, 512 and 256 px into pieces/4x, pieces/2x and pieces/1x, named wP, wN, wB, wR, wQ, wK, bP … bK. Set pieces.source to pieces/{res}/{piece}.webp, resolutions to ["1x","2x","4x"], baseSize to 256 and anchor.y to where the foot sits in the image. Do not bake a shadow. They stand as billboards in the 3D scene with a soft shadow. For animated pieces render one horizontal strip of frames per piece and set pieces.frames and pieces.idle.style to frames.
5. Zip the contents of the folder (theme.json at the root of the archive, not inside a subfolder), rename the file to .cctheme and import it. If something is wrong the import tells you exactly what.
Limits: 64 MB per archive, images up to 8192 px and 36 megapixels, png / webp / jpg / svg only. Custom 3D meshes (glTF) and shaders are not part of format 1: a mesh loader needs its own security review, so today only the procedural Staunton model and sprites are accepted.
